purpose: An ordinary verified participant can explicitly trust a device for a bounded period and inspect, name or remove their own trusted devices in the development entry.

implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-178 extends the existing private DeviceAssurance Resource and Session management page with participant-owned device trust. Master Gate corrections bound the trusted set and use eligible copy. A scoped Audit insert fault proves grant rollback and cookie suppression.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Audit owns the selected E2 obligations. The source transaction owns the grant and removal. Audit evidence cannot grant device trust.

ash.caller_boundary: Private actions used by Identity under the Account lock. The browser receives only a narrow owner projection.
Identity establishes the selected obligation inside the source transaction through the Audit interface.

arguments: List, grant with a fresh random 32-byte artifact, rename with a bounded name, or remove by identifier.
returns: A self-only list, a granted device projection or outcome.
Generic denial or uncertain transaction result.
side_effects: Records due expiry. Explicit consent and manual removal establish selected evidence atomically.
caller_constraints: Revalidates current Account, Token, Session and ordinary eligibility under lock. The browser only submits the grant after CSRF-protected consent.

request_flow.summary: The existing Session management page loads routed bilingual copy, reads only the presenting Account's current trust and issues a random, encrypted, Session-bound consent form proof.

The consent POST verifies CSRF and the ten-minute proof. Identity creates a pending record and moves it to trusted within the source transaction. A confirmed grant sets the scoped Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie with the remaining expiry.
Identity matches the cookie by SHA-256 and projects device id, name, expiry and whether the artifact matches. Explicit removal and name/save use the target's Account-scoped id.
A name save with an uncertain result redirects to an authoritative GET of the localized inventory. The refreshed form presents the name Identity currently reads.

guards: Explicit consent and current ordinary Account, bearer, Session and device deadline.
side_effects: Durable consent row and selected grant obligation commit together. Trust lasts 30 days.

guards: The application clock is sampled after acquiring current authority. Expired trust is excluded from inventory and persisted as expired on observation.
side_effects: The digest remains bound and cannot be reused.

guards: The current owner confirms removal, or Identity commits an Account security invalidation.
side_effects: Trust ends. Manual removal records selected Audit and leaves the Session active. Existing Account security transitions record their own selected evidence.

security_invariants.summary: All operations require a currently usable ordinary Account Session and bearer. Active governed grants deny this participant path.
Raw artifacts are carried by the browser only. Identity stores a hash, Account security version, name and deadline. The browser receives no raw Artifact in rendered HTML.
Trust supplies no login, idle or absolute Session lifetime, MFA or high-risk step-up authority.

concurrency.summary: Operations hold the Account lock, then the presenting Token and Session locks before device access. Account-wide invalidations serialize on the same Account lock.

The Account lock serializes the ten-record capacity check with new grants. Each trusted-record read is limited to ten and uses the Account-scoped partial index, which excludes terminal history. The reconciliation pass retires only that bounded set. Expired and stale-version rows become terminal and free capacity. Terminal history remains available for fingerprint replay denial.

idempotency_retry.summary: Replays of one current consent artifact return the original row and deadline. Expired, revoked and stale-version artifacts cannot re-grant. A new device requires fresh consent.
Repeated removal returns already ended without a duplicate Audit obligation. A foreign or missing id returns the same denial.
Replaying an existing current artifact at capacity returns the original row and expiry. One new artifact can claim the last slot, and expiry permits a later fresh grant.

failure_recovery.summary: The source write rolls back if Audit cannot establish the obligation. An uncertain write result is handled by reading the current inventory. No cookie is issued before a confirmed grant.

Device state is reconstructed from PostgreSQL. Existing source security writes terminate trust before commitment. A database down-migration after real use cannot narrow the Audit check while selected evidence remains and would remove names. Use a forward correction to retain evidence.

cases: Consent, duplicate replay, cross-Account denial, rename, removal, fresh consent, expiry, concurrent consent and Audit rejection.
Global sign-out invalidates a device issued through the owner interface.
Separate database connections compete for the last of ten slots, an existing artifact still replays, and expiry frees capacity without deleting or reviving the expired record.
tests.proves: Durable Account scoping, terminal states, convergence, rollback and selected E2.
tests.limits: Elapsed time is represented by a synthetic persisted deadline fixture.

cases: Chromium consent, rename, keyboard confirmation, fresh inventory and surviving Session.
A connection-scoped Audit insertion rejection reaches the real source write, leaves zero DeviceAssurance rows and sends no cookie. The same consent succeeds once the fault is removed.
tests.proves: The real development endpoint renders eligible localized copy and carries the opaque artifact in a private cookie.
tests.limits: Synthetic accounts and a loopback browser.

cases: Compromise hold terminates a previously granted device.
tests.proves: The existing security hold source transaction revokes participant trust.
tests.limits: Uses the approved synthetic Support and participant fixture.

safe_extensions.summary: Keep any future browser or delivery extension behind the Identity interface and revalidate the current Account, Session, grant posture and deadline.

reuse.summary: Reuses private Ash DeviceAssurance, current Session authority, Account-wide invalidation, Audit source obligations and the approved bilingual packet. No new dependency is needed.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not treat the cookie as authentication, bypass step-up, set trust silently, log raw artifacts, or use a reversible state change to re-enroll a terminal artifact.

proof_limitations: Synthetic DEV/TEST only. Production activation, privileged device policy and optional login convenience are outside this increment.

sources.symbol: suspected compromise terminates participant device trust
